intro: Hopes and good wishes: ojalá, espero que, and the short wishes that begin with que.
p.ojalá.consejo: It always takes the subjunctive: «ojalá haga sol». It is a word of Arabic origin.
p.esperar que.consejo: With another person, subjunctive: «espero que vengas». With the same one, infinitive: «espero venir».
p.que te mejores.consejo: You say it to someone ill. It is a wish, so it has «que» and the subjunctive.
p.que aproveche.consejo: You say it when passing people eating. The v sounds like b: «a-pro-BE-che».
p.que tengas suerte.consejo: It fits before an exam. You can also say «buena suerte».
p.que lo pases bien.consejo: «Pasarlo bien» means to enjoy yourself. With «usted» it would be «que lo pase bien».
p.que descanses.consejo: It comes from «descansar». The c sounds like k before a: «des-KAN-ses».
p.que cumplas muchos más.consejo: It is the long form of «felicidades» at a birthday: you wish many more years.
p.enhorabuena.consejo: The h is silent: «e-no-ra-BWE-na». It is used for achievements: an exam, a job.
p.felicidades.consejo: It works for a birthday and for almost anything. It is always plural.
p.aprobar.consejo: It changes o to ue: «apruebo», «apruebes». The opposite is «suspender».
p.examen.consejo: The x sounds «ks»: «ek-SA-men». The plural is «exámenes», with an accent.
p.llover.consejo: It changes o to ue: «llueve», «llueva». It only has the él / ella form.
b1.texto:
**Ojalá** + subjunctive expresses a wish about the present or the future: **ojalá haga** sol, **ojalá apruebes**.

**Espero que** + subjunctive speaks about what someone else will do: espero que **vengas**. With the same subject, use the infinitive: espero **venir**.

A phrase with **que** alone is also a wish, without saying «espero»:

- ¡**Que te mejores**! (to someone ill)
- ¡**Que aproveche**! (to someone eating)
- ¡**Que tengas** suerte! · ¡**Que lo pases** bien! · ¡**Que descanses**!

**Felicidades** works for a birthday and for almost anything. **Enhorabuena** is used for an achievement: an exam, a new job.
b2.f0.texto: Tomorrow I have my driving test.
b2.f2.texto: I hope you pass on the first try.
b2.f3.texto: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
b2.f4.texto: I hope the examiner is nice.
b2.f5.texto: I hope not to be nervous.
b2.f7.texto: Afterwards I'll call you and tell you everything.
b4.texto:
There are three ways to express a wish:

- **Ojalá + subjunctive**: ojalá haga sol · ojalá llueva poco.
- **Espero que + subjunctive**: espero que vengas. With the same subject: espero **llegar** pronto.
- **Que + subjunctive**: a short wish with no verb in front. ¡Que te mejores! ¡Que lo pases bien!

With **ojalá** you can add **que** without changing the meaning: ojalá **que** apruebes.

The «tú» form is for friends and family. With «usted» or «ustedes» the verb changes: ¡que lo pase bien! · ¡que lo pasen bien!
b4.e0.texto: I hope it is sunny tomorrow.
b4.e2.texto: I hope it doesn't rain on Saturday.
b5.f0.texto: A grey light comes in through the window and wakes Lucía.
b5.f1.texto: In the kitchen, the coffee bubbles with a warm murmur.
b5.f2.texto: The fine rain taps the windowpanes with fingers of water.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía goes over the road signs in a notebook of crumpled pages.
b5.f4.texto: Her mother leaves a yellow note on the table.
b5.f5.texto: The note says three words in big, round letters.
b5.f6.texto: Lucía reads them out loud and smiles.
b5.f7.texto: Outside, the wind shakes the wet branches of the trees.
b5.f8.texto: In the car, the examiner looks at his watch calmly.
b5.f9.texto: Lucía breathes deeply, grips the wheel and waits for a sign.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Hace» is the ordinary present. After «ojalá» comes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Ojalá» asks for the subjunctive: from «hago», «haga».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Ojalá» asks for a conjugated verb, not the infinitive.
b6.pregunta: You hope for good weather. Which form is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is said to someone about to eat, not to a sick person.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes! You wish her to get better: «que te mejores».
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is for a birthday, not for the flu.
b7.pregunta: Your friend has the flu. What do you wish her?
b8.o0.refuerzo: The subjunctive needs a different subject. Here it is you.
b8.o1.refuerzo: «Llegas» is for «tú», and the subject is «yo».
b8.pregunta: You yourself hope to arrive. What is missing?
b9.traduccion: I hope you have a good trip
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done! It is the wish for someone about to eat.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is said when going to bed.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Enhorabuena» congratulates an achievement, not a meal.
b10.pregunta: Neighbours sit down to eat. What do you say?
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Aprobar» changes o to ue and asks for the subjunctive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Apruebas» is the ordinary present, with no wish.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Ojalá» asks for a conjugated verb, not the infinitive.
b12.pregunta: You hope Lucía succeeds. Which form is missing?
p.suerte.consejo: Say «tener suerte» for luck and «buena suerte» to wish it. It is feminine: «la suerte».
p.apruebes.consejo: Subjunctive of «aprobar» for tú. The o becomes ue: «apruebo», «apruebes».
p.llueva.consejo: Subjunctive of «llover». The ll sounds y and the v sounds b: «YWE-ba».
p.examinador.consejo: It comes from «examinar». The x sounds ks. A woman is «la examinadora».
p.llamo.consejo: Present of «llamar». The ll sounds y: «YA-mo». «Me llamo» means «my name is».
p.cuento.consejo: Present of «contar», which means to tell and to count. The o becomes ue: «cuento», «cuentas».
p.haga.consejo: Subjunctive of «hacer» for yo, él or usted. The h is silent: «A-ga». «Haga sol» is «it is sunny».
p.pases.consejo: Subjunctive of «pasar». In «lo pases bien», «pasarlo» means to have a good time.
p.burbujea.consejo: From «burbuja» (bubble). The j sounds h and the stress is on «HE».
p.murmullo.consejo: The ll sounds y: «mur-MU-yo». It is also used for water, leaves or voices.
p.repasa.consejo: The initial r sounds strong: «rre-PA-sa». It means to review what you already know.
p.señales.consejo: The ñ sounds ny: «se-NYA-les». The singular is «señal». Traffic signs are «señales de tráfico».
p.cuaderno.consejo: Not to be mixed up with «cuadro» (picture). Both start with «cua», which sounds «kwa».
p.arrugadas.consejo: From «arruga» (wrinkle). The rr sounds strong: «a-rru-GA-das». Feminine plural, for «hojas».
p.sacude.consejo: The c sounds k before u: «sa-KU-de». You «sacudes» a rug, a branch or the snow off your boots.
p.agarra.consejo: The rr in the middle sounds strong: «a-GA-rra». It means to hold something firmly.
p.volante.consejo: The v sounds b: «bo-LAN-te». You «conduces» a car holding the «volante».
p.viaje.consejo: The v sounds b and the j sounds h: «BYA-he». «Buen viaje» is the wish for a trip.
